It remains unclear, however, to what extent the use of chemothera- py combined with radiotherapy could have an additive effect on the risk of secondary leukaemias, and how dose and treatment regimen influence this effect.3 Similarly, the role of combined modality treatment in the development of secondary solid tu- mours has not been defined, even though the radiation-enhanc- ing effect of some antineoplastics is known and used in chemo- radiation regimens for this reason.4 In many cases the risk of secondary malignancy is far less than that of undertreating, or of failing to treat, the primary disease.2,4 However, secondary malignancies may be more resistant to treatment and more aggressive than primary disease,3,19 and the risk of inducing malignant neoplasia is certainly a consideration in the use of alkylating agents and podophyllotoxin derivatives to treat non-malignant disease,3 and is an increasing challenge in the design of suitable treatment regimens for primary neoplastic disease. 1.
